Consider the following 12×12 integer matrix A.

A =
[  1   3   0   2   0  -2   0   1   6   0   1   0 ]
[ -1  -3   1  -5  -2   4  -1  -2  -7   0   0   0 ]
[  0   0  -1   3   2  -2   2   2   2   0  -2   0 ]
[  0   0  -1   3   2  -2   0   1   3  -1  -1   2 ]
[  1   3   1  -1  -2   0  -1   1   8   0   2   1 ]
[ -1  -3   0  -2   0   2   0  -2  -9   2   2  -3 ]
[  0   0   1  -3  -2   2   0  -1  -3   0  -1  -1 ]
[  0   0   1  -3  -2   2  -1  -2  -4   2   4  -3 ]
[ -1  -3   1  -5  -2   4   0   0  -3  -2  -4   3 ]
[ -1  -3   1  -5  -2   4  -2  -2  -5  -1  -1   2 ]
[  1   3  -1   5   2  -4   2   3   8  -1  -2   1 ]
[ -1  -3   0  -2   0   2   1  -1  -8   2   1  -3 ]

Find the rank r of A and its pivot columns: the columns that are not linear combinations of the columns to their left (equivalently, the columns containing the leading 1s of the reduced row echelon form of A). Give r followed by the 1-based indices of the pivot columns in increasing order, as one comma-separated list of integers (r, c_1, …, c_r).

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
